name: colonies-03-wcm-rss-leak
title: Inner EcoliWCM RSS leak — localize and fix
description:
colonies-02 refuted per-cell-rss-drift-bounded: a single EcoliWCM grows RSS
~7.7 MB/sim-s (emitter-independent), reaching ~19 GB before its first division
and OOM-killing the sequential colony at 27.5 GB. Under Ray the leak moves into
the per-cell actors (~34 GB at 2 cells), so process parallelism lifts the
GIL/compute ceiling but RAM becomes the binding constraint, making the
cells-per-node budget untrustworthy and blocking HPC deployment. This study
localizes the leak to a named allocation site and fixes it so per-cell RSS
stays bounded over a natural-division lifetime.

baseline.name: single-ecoliwcm-long
baseline.note:
Profile a SINGLE EcoliWCM over a long pre-division run (~2500s) — no
colony, no pymunk — so the leak is isolated to the inner whole-cell
composite, not the colony wiring. colonies-02 already showed it is
transport- and emitter-independent.

purpose.question:
Where does the ~7.7 MB/sim-s RSS growth in a single EcoliWCM come from,
and can it be fixed so per-cell RSS stays bounded (sawtooth around a
flat baseline) across a natural-division lifetime — unblocking the
colonies HPC sizing?
purpose.mechanism:
Localized (2026-06-15): the leak is the inner per-cell RAMEmitter, not
chromosome_history. Each embedded cell's inner Composite (built by baseline()
in the EcoliWCM bridge) gets a default RAMEmitter whose no-override branch
(v2ecoli/composites/_helpers.py) captures `bulk` (~25k-molecule array) plus
four unique-molecule node arrays (full_chromosome / active_replisome /
active_RNAP / chromosome_domain) every tick into an unbounded history list
(RAMEmitter.update -> history.append(tree_copy)). That history is never read
(the bridge reads composite.state directly), so it is pure leak matching the
~7.7 MB/sim-s. This corrects colonies-02's "emitter-independent" call: the
no-emitter probe there nulled only the outer colony emitter, while each cell's
inner emitter kept accumulating.
Fix: a `_RAM_EMITTER_CAPTURE='minimal'` mode in _helpers.py (global_time +
listeners only) that the bridge sets for embedded cells; default stays 'full'
for standalone callers that read the in-RAM tree. (Other candidates ruled out
as dominant: chromosome_history append (bridge.py:243) is unbounded but small;
unique-molecule array growth is legitimate biomass, not a leak.)
purpose.expected_outcome:
A tracemalloc/gc profile attributes the bulk of growth to one or two named
sites. After the fix, a single-cell ~2500s run holds RSS within a bounded band
(no monotonic climb), and a re-run of colonies-02's seq-1cell-4div completes 3
generations without OOM while leaving the biology unchanged (first division
still tick 2338, masses within RNG).

build_tasks.motivation:
Fixing before localizing risks treating a symptom. colonies-02 proved
the leak is real, emitter- and transport-independent; this pins it to a
site.
build_tasks.action:
Run sims/profile_leak.py: a single EcoliWCM for ~2500 ticks with
tracemalloc snapshots every ~200 ticks, recording top allocation deltas,
gc object-type counts, len(chromosome_history), and inner-composite
state size. Commit profiling/leak_profile.csv + a top-sites table as
evidence. Decide the fix from the data.

build_tasks.motivation: Bounded per-cell RSS is the gate condition for HPC deployment.
build_tasks.action:
Apply the smallest fix the profile justifies (e.g. cap/disable
chromosome_history when unused; release inner-composite per-tick
retention). Keep it behind a flag if it changes recorded outputs.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
colonies-02 recorded the leak (done). Proceed once a profile localizes
>=~80% of the growth to named site(s).
pipeline_gate.blocks_until_resolved:
colonies-04-hpc-deployment stays blocked until per-cell RSS is bounded
over a natural-division lifetime — otherwise any cells-per-node budget
is a lower bound that OOMs in practice.

simulation_set.name: profile-1cell-predivision
simulation_set.description:
Single EcoliWCM (no colony/pymunk), ~2500 ticks (pre-first-division),
tracemalloc + gc profiling. Localization run.

simulation_set.name: postfix-seq-1cell-4div
simulation_set.description:
After the fix, re-run colonies-02's sequential natural-division colony
to confirm 3 generations complete without OOM and RSS stays bounded.
(Run via colonies-02 sims/run.py on the fixed branch.)

behavior_tests.name: leak-localized
behavior_tests.description:
A profiling run attributes >=~80% of RSS growth to one or two named
allocation sites (so the fix is targeted, not speculative).

behavior_tests.name: per-cell-rss-bounded-after-fix
behavior_tests.description:
Post-fix single-cell ~2500s run holds RSS in a bounded band (no
monotonic ~MB/sim-s climb); colonies-02's seq-1cell-4div completes
>=3 generations without OOM.

behavior_tests.name: biology-unchanged-by-fix
behavior_tests.description:
The fix does not alter recorded biology: first division still at tick
2338, per-cell mass at division within RNG of the colonies-02 run.

findings.statement:
The colonies-02 ~7.7 MB/sim-s per-cell RSS leak is the inner per-cell
RAMEmitter, not chromosome_history and not "emitter-independent". Each
embedded cell's inner Composite (built by baseline() in the EcoliWCM
bridge) gets a default RAMEmitter whose no-override branch
(_helpers.py) captures `bulk` (~25k-molecule array) + four unique-
molecule node arrays every tick into an unbounded history list that is
never read. colonies-02's no-emitter probe nulled only the outer colony
emitter, missing the per-cell inner emitters.
findings.evidence:
Live profiler measured the inner RAMEmitter history at ~5.15 MB/row,
growing 1:1 with ticks (9.9 MB @ 2 rows -> 9324 MB @ 1802 rows), tracking
the RSS climb. Confirmed by reading process_bigraph Emitter.inputs() ==
config['emit'] (the emitter only stores its emit_schema ports).

findings.verdict: PASS (single-cell bridge path); multi-cell colony no-OOM = confirmatory follow-up
findings.statement:
Setting the inner RAMEmitter to 'minimal' capture (global_time +
listeners only) for embedded cells bounds per-cell RSS. A single
EcoliWCM built through the bridge (set_ram_emitter_capture('minimal'))
holds RSS essentially flat.
findings.evidence:
Bridge-path profile_leak.py (commit bd1a11fe) RSS: 1.3 GB @ 21 min ->
1.7 GB @ 48 min -> 1.9 GB @ 62 min (~0.25 MB/s, legitimate cell growth),
vs the unfixed path +24 GB by tick 1800 (~7.7 MB/s). ~30x reduction;
no monotonic emitter-driven climb.
findings.next_action:
Confirmatory (not load-bearing): run colonies-02 seq-1cell-4div to full
duration on the mini to show the multi-cell colony completes >=3
generations without OOM. The fix is per-cell, so N bounded cells follow.

findings.statement:
The fix only narrows what the inner RAMEmitter records (a read-only
history sink); the emit_schema does not feed back into simulation state,
so division timing and masses are unchanged by construction. The full
colony re-run (first division still tick 2338) is the empirical
re-confirmation, deferred with the no-OOM run above.

The inner-RAMEmitter fix (F-01/F-02) is real and bounds a single bare WCM,
but it is not the dominant leak for a multi-cell colony. Re-running
colonies-02 on current main with all three contributory fixes live
(#239 inner emitter, emit_cells=False outer emitter, viva-munk #11 pymunk
shape churn) still leaks ~0.5-1 MB/tick/cell: the count=6 plateau climbed
5.1 -> 22.3 GB at a constant 6 cells and OOMs ~gen 3, unchanged from before
the fixes.
findings.evidence:
tracemalloc(4) over 150 ticks at 2 forced-division cells: RSS climbed
1396 -> 1586 MB (+1.3 MB/tick), leak reproduced, yet tracemalloc
accounted for only ~1-2 MB of retained Python allocations (largest single
site +0.08 MB; all transient WCM compute: counts_deriver/translation_deriver
np.bincount, scipy-sparse .dot). So the dominant allocator is C-level /
native (numpy/scipy array buffers or a C-extension retaining or fragmenting
memory), invisible to tracemalloc (it tracks only CPython's allocator, not
numpy's). gc object-count scans likewise found only small symptoms
(pymunk Segments -> #11), not the megabytes.
findings.next_action:
Needs a NATIVE heap profiler (macOS `leaks`/`malloc_history` with
MALLOC_STACK_LOGGING, or jemalloc/tcmalloc heap profiling), not Python
tooling. Until then the colony is RAM-blocked for multi-generation runs and
colonies-04-hpc-deployment stays blocked. The 3 Python-level fixes remain
valid wins (merged).

findings.verdict: OPEN — root cause localized to the Numba/LLVM JIT layer (tracked: #253)
findings.statement:
The dominant per-tick growth is native and localized to the LLVM/Numba JIT
layer. A controlled staged run (colonies-02 sims/mem_measure.py) shows
numpy-object bytes flat within each cell-count plateau while native memory
climbs (decomposition figure), and macOS `leaks` (MallocStackLogging) finds
the true unreachable leak with stacks in llvmlite's LLVM pass pipeline
(LLVMPY_buildFunctionSimplificationPipeline). So the WCM's JIT compilation
is the source, not the emitters (#239), the outer emitter (emit_cells), the
pymunk shapes (viva-munk #11), or a retained numpy array.
findings.evidence:
leaks @2cells/400ticks: ~846 MB live, ~13 MB true leak, top stacks all
LLVM PassBuilder (GVN/JumpThreading/LoopUnswitch/LICM). numpy-bytes delta
~0 within plateaus; tracemalloc <2 MB of a +151 MB/300-tick growth.
Figures: colonies-02 charts/03_memory_decomposition.svg (native vs numpy),
charts/01_rss_vs_tick_by_ncells.svg (per-tick slope by N).
findings.next_action:
Tracked as engineering issue #253: find where the WCM (re)compiles @njit
functions per tick/cell and make them module-level + cache=True so they
compile once and are shared; confirm with NUMBA_DISABLE_JIT=1 flattening the
growth. Separately, the per-cell footprint (each cell = an independent
baseline composite loading its own sim_data, ~1+ GB/cell, colonies-02
charts/02) is a distinct, bounded RAM limiter worth a shared-sim_data design.

derived.insight:
The colonies-02 ~7.7 MB/sim-s per-cell RSS leak is the inner per-cell
RAMEmitter, not chromosome_history and not "emitter-independent". Each
embedded cell's inner Composite (built by baseline() in the EcoliWCM
bridge) gets a default RAMEmitter whose no-override branch
(_helpers.py) captures `bulk` (~25k-molecule array) + four unique-
molecule node arrays every tick into an unbounded history list that is
never read. colonies-02's no-emitter probe nulled only the outer colony
emitter, missing the per-cell inner emitters.
